title: Connected-limit preservation by the sheafified site left adjoint
statement: Work in the small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor]. Assume that fibre products and equalizers exist in $\mathcal C$ and that $i$ preserves them, meaning that their image cones have the corresponding universal properties in $\mathcal D$. Write $R:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ for precomposition, $RG(U)=G(iU)$, on sheaves of sets. Let $L:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be the sheafified presheaf left adjoint $LF=(i_pF)^\#$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], where $\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Then $L\dashv R$, and $L$ preserves fibre products and equalizers of sheaves of sets. No terminal object in either underlying site, and no preservation of the terminal sheaf by $L$, is assumed.

source.place: Tags 00XR (lemma-when-shriek), assertions (1),(2), and 00XS (lemma-preserve-equalizers), hypotheses (a)--(c) and conclusion.

proof.text: Continuity gives that $RG=G\circ i$ is a sheaf, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] with values in sets: $L\dashv R$, and $(i_pF)(V)=\operatorname{colim}_{J_V}F(U)$, where $J_V=I_V^{op}$ and $I_V$ has objects $(U,\phi:V\to iU)$ and arrows $a:(U,\phi)\to(U\prime,\phi\prime)$ with $i(a)\phi=\phi\prime$. These categories are small, since the objects and arrows of both sites form sets in the chosen universe.

Check the common-source span condition for $J_V$. A span with common source in $J_V$ is a cospan $(U\prime,\phi\prime)\xrightarrow{a}(U,\phi)\xleftarrow{b}(U\prime\prime,\phi\prime\prime)$ in $I_V$. Take $P=U\prime\times_U U\prime\prime$. The image pullback gives a unique $\psi:V\to iP$ with projections $\phi\prime,\phi\prime\prime$. Its projection arrows in $I_V$ commute because $a p_1=b p_2$. Reversing arrows gives the required cocone in $J_V$. This uses only the assumed universal property of the image pullback.

For condition (b), parallel arrows in $J_V$ reverse to $a,b:(U,\phi)\rightrightarrows(U\prime,\phi\prime)$ in $I_V$. Let $e:E\to U$ equalize $a,b$. Since $i(a)\phi=i(b)\phi=\phi\prime$ and $i(e)$ is an equalizer, there is a unique $\psi:V\to iE$ with $i(e)\psi=\phi$. Thus $e:(E,\psi)\to(U,\phi)$ is an arrow of $I_V$ equalizing $a,b$. Its opposite coequalizes the given pair in $J_V$. Neither check required $I_V$ to have any objects.

For any presheaf diagram $F_1\to F_0\leftarrow F_2$, its fibre product has sections $F_1(U)\times_{F_0(U)}F_2(U)$; an equalizer has sections $\operatorname{Eq}(f_U,g_U)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-finite-limits-objectwise]. For each $V$, steps 2 and 3 verify precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-almost-filtered-set-colimits]. Apply its two canonical bijections to the functors $(U,\phi)\mapsto F_j(U)$ on $J_V$. By the comma-colimit formula in step 1 these are the comparisons for $i_p$ at $V$. They commute with restriction in $V$: precomposing $\phi$ and then applying a diagram projection gives the same colimit representative as applying the projection first. Consequently $i_p$ preserves fibre products and equalizers as presheaves.

Now start with a fibre-product or equalizer diagram of sheaves on $\mathcal C$. Its limit as a presheaf is the sheaf limit by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. Step 4 identifies its image under $i_p$ with the corresponding presheaf limit on $\mathcal D$. Sheafification preserves this finite limit by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], so sheafifying the comparison proves that $L=(i_p-)^\#$ preserves the given sheaf limit. Together with step 1 this proves every assertion. The empty comma category causes no exception: both comparisons in the categorical lemma are between empty sets.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00XR and 00XS, expanding the two universal-property checks of 00X4 and citing the set-colimit input 002Y.
